problem: Traditional 3D LiDAR localization and navigation systems cannot accurately position an inspection robot around a target object, and existing language-driven semantic navigation methods lack generalizability, stability and ease of deployment for inspection tasks.
motivation: Inspection robots need to understand natural language commands and navigate precisely to named target objects, then report what they see in a user-friendly way. Reliable positioning near the object and easy deployment without complex initialization are needed in practice.
key_idea: Build a LiDAR-plus-RGB 3D semantic map encoded as plain text for an LLM that decodes commands into inspection primitives, use a target cost gradient for target point and pose selection, and use a VLM plus LLM to describe the scene on arrival.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract suggests that a text-encoded semantic map lets an LLM ground commands, and that a semantic-aware target cost gradient fixes the poor positioning around objects that LiDAR-only navigation suffers from.
method: Semantic mapping: LiDAR builds a geometric depth map; RGB images give object categories that are fused with depth into a 3D semantic map.
Text map encoding: the 3D semantic map is encoded as plain text so the LLM can interpret the environment.
LLM command decoding: an LLM constrained by system initial prompts converts human commands into inspection primitives.
Low-level planner: the inspection primitives drive the robot's low-level planner for task execution.
Target cost gradient: optimizes target point selection and attitude (pose) control near target objects in the semantic map.
Scene description: on arrival a VLM describes the scene, and the LLM simplifies it into a user-friendly response.

setting.backbone: LLM (unspecified) + VLM (unspecified) for command decoding and scene description; LiDAR-based geometric planner
setting.training_data: Not stated in the abstract; appears to use pre-trained LLM/VLM with prompting
setting.action_space: Low-level planner driven by inspection primitives (target point and pose)

numbers_note: abstract only; the abstract reports a 46.9% improvement in SR and a 58.3% increase in SPL over SOTA, but no absolute values
results: On 18 indoor Matterport3D scenes, L-SNI improves SR by 46.9% and SPL by 58.3% over existing SOTA solutions, and shows better target image understanding. It can also be deployed on real robots without complex initialization.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so details on baselines, absolute metrics and the LLM/VLM used are unknown.
Relies on LiDAR plus RGB semantic mapping quality and on a text encoding of the map.
